title: Declarative Row Edits
doc: CKF Hard Mode - declarative row edits.
The rule engine itself is configured by ckf.hardmode.rules.json and the
ckf.hardmode.d/*.csv overlays, which this schema deliberately does NOT
cover - they are bulk table authoring with their own grammar and their own
editor, the spreadsheet. See SCHEMA-FORMAT.md, 'What the schema
deliberately does not cover'. The one exception is
ckf.hardmode.d/MissionPowerLevelModel.generated.json, which is a schema
output rather than an input and belongs to teampl.schema.json.
So the five keys here are the wholesale switch plus the diagnostics. In 3.0
they moved out of the [ModelRules] section of ckf.hardmode.cfg and into the
"modelrules" section of ckf.hardmode.json; the section is new in 3.0 and has
no 2.x sidecar behind it, which is what targets.legacyJson: null records. Five
more were removed in 2.12.0:
EnableRowCloning, CloneServeById, CloneFreshInstances and CompiledAccessors
are hardcoded on, and CloneServeOnBulkReads is hardcoded OFF with its branch
deleted - nothing during play enumerates a whole table, and an append
landing after the game has already built from the list cost a mission load
in Run 42.
THE WRITABLE-COLUMN PROBE IS NOT A DUPLICATE of CKF Data Dump's WriteProbe.
Checked 2026-08-31 against that plugin's sources: the two are disjoint on
every axis. This one probes content tables discovered from the rules, every
scalar property, at first materialization, and always restores in a finally.
WriteProbe writes four hardcoded save columns plus Credits on the first turn
tick and deliberately never restores. This one answers 'does the setter keep
the value' - the alias and Adjusted* case where a rule fails silently.
WriteProbe answers 'does an Update* persist'.
uiDoc: Retune the game's talents, equipment, monster and character base stats. The rules themselves live in the rule file and the CSV overlays and are edited in a spreadsheet, not on this page.

Tracing is for confirming a rule did what you meant without hunting for the effect in-game: it logs the first few rows each rule changes, one line per column, before and after. Three to five is enough to see a curve produce different values at different levels. It logs a line per row, so turn it off again for a normal session.

The writable-column probe is for the other kind of failure. Some columns take a write and then recompute the value and discard yours, and a rule against one of those fails silently. The probe finds them. Turn it on for a single launch when a rule is not landing, read the report, and turn it off again.

fields.label: Apply rules
fields.doc: Apply declarative record edits from ckf.hardmode.rules.json - talents, equipment, monster and character base stats.

fields.label: Trace first N rows per rule
fields.doc: Log the first N rows each rule changes, one line per column, as before -> after. This is how you confirm a rule, a curve, a clamp or a clone actually did what you meant without hunting for the effect in-game. 0 is off. 3 to 5 is enough to see a curve produce different values at different power levels. It logs per row, so leave it off for a normal session.

fields.label: Probe writable columns
fields.uiDoc: Write a report of which columns actually accept a write. Some columns take a value and then recompute it, discarding yours, and a rule against one of those fails silently. The probe writes a test value to one row per table, reads it back and puts the original straight back. It's worth a launch when a rule is not landing.
fields.doc: Write a report of which columns actually accept a write. Some setters exist but recompute their value and discard yours - the unsuffixed weapon stats are aliases for the selected firing mode, and the talent Adjusted* columns are computed - and a rule against one of those fails silently. The probe writes a test value onto one materialized row per table, reads it back, and puts the original value straight back. It is a write on the game's hot path, so it is off by default and worth turning on for one launch when a rule is not landing.

fields.label: Extra tables to probe
fields.doc: Extra tables to probe, beyond the ones your rules already target (which are probed automatically). A JSON array of strings; the 'Model' suffix is optional.

fields.label: Probe report path
fields.doc: Where to write the writable-column report. Blank means BepInEx/ckf-hardmode/writable_columns.csv. Set a path you own if the game lives under Program Files and the write is blocked.
